requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a MAX_DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: The frame consists of a Type field followed by a Maximum Data field, both encoded as variable-length integers.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not reverse the specified field order or omit either field.
requirements.why_checkable: A serialized MAX_DATA frame can be parsed to verify the presence, encoding class, and order of its two fields.

requirements.condition: When encoding or recognizing a MAX_DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or recognize the variable-length Type field as 0x10.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A frame with a Type value other than 0x10 must not be treated as a MAX_DATA frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded frame type is directly comparable with the fixed value 0x10.

requirements.quote:
Maximum Data:  A variable-length integer indicating the maximum
      amount of data that can be sent on the entire connection, in units
      of bytes.
requirements.condition: When encoding, parsing, or applying the Maximum Data field of a MAX_DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and decode Maximum Data as a variable-length integer representing the connection-wide data limit in bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The field must not be interpreted as a per-stream limit or in units other than bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can inspect the field encoding and verify that its decoded value is applied as a byte-denominated connection-wide limit.

requirements.condition: When accounting for use of the connection-wide maximum data limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Count all data sent in STREAM frames toward the limit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not exclude STREAM-frame data from connection-level flow-control accounting.
requirements.why_checkable: Flow-control accounting can be observed while STREAM frames carrying data are processed.

requirements.condition: When determining whether the sender remains within the receiver's advertised connection-wide limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the sum of the final sizes of every stream, including streams in terminal states, at or below the receiver-advertised value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The sum of stream final sizes must not exceed the receiver-advertised value, and terminal-state streams must not be omitted from the sum.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's stream final sizes and advertised limit can be inspected and summed, including completed or otherwise terminal streams.

requirements.quote:
endpoint MUST terminate a connection with an error of type
   FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR if it receives more data than the maximum data
   value that it has sent.  This includes violations of remembered
   limits in Early Data; see Section 7.4.1.
requirements.condition: If an endpoint receives more data than the maximum data value it has sent, including a violation of a remembered limit during Early Data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not continue the connection after detecting this flow-control violation.
requirements.error_behavior: Terminate with an error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can send data beyond the endpoint's advertised or remembered maximum and verify connection termination with FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
